identity.title: SWINGARENA: Adversarial Programming Arena for Long-context GitHub Issue Solving

problem.claim: Evaluate LLMs on long-context GitHub issue solving in realistic software-development workflows.

gap.claim: Traditional static benchmarks do not model collaborative software iteration with patch submission, review, test creation, and CI verification.

contributions.claim: Introduces SwingArena, an adversarial arena pairing LLM submitters that generate patches with reviewers that create tests and verify patches through CI.

Introduces a retrieval-augmented code-generation module that retrieves syntactically and semantically relevant snippets from large codebases across C++, Python, Rust, and Go for long-context evaluation.
Defines a scalable and extensible approach for CI-driven evaluation across diverse tasks and contexts under token limits.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish SwingArena from static benchmarks by adversarially modeling collaborative, iterative, CI-based software development and adding RACG for long-context code retrieval.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on over 400 real-world GitHub issues selected from 2,300 issues.
The authors report that GPT-4o excelled at aggressive patch generation, while DeepSeek and Gemini prioritized correctness in CI validation.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames realistic software-workflow evaluation as the target.
SwingArena replaces static evaluation with submitter–reviewer interaction and CI-based patch verification.
RACG retrieves relevant code across four languages while respecting token limitations.
Experiments on more than 400 selected GitHub issues compare model tendencies in patch generation and CI validation.
The authors characterize the resulting methodology as scalable and extensible for realistic CI-driven evaluation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates patch generation from test creation and CI verification, assigning them to interacting submitter and reviewer roles.

lessons.interpretation: Decomposing evaluation into adversarial roles can expose trade-offs hidden by a single-pass score.
lessons.application: Design an issue-solving benchmark with separate patch-author and test/reviewer agents, and report generation and CI outcomes independently.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when the research question concerns only isolated code synthesis or when reliable automated tests cannot be constructed.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative performance metrics, baselines, or statistical details for the reported model comparison.
Selection criteria for the 400 issues, RACG retrieval procedure, CI setup, and meaning of “correctness” are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independently verified effectiveness, reproducibility, or priority of the claimed novelty.
